EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the classic Raman pattern of a monosubstituted benzene bearing a carbonyl chloride.  Key evidence:  
• Very strong ring-breathing band at 1009 cm⁻¹ and aromatic C–H stretch at 3081 cm⁻¹, together with doublet C=C stretches at 1593/1605 cm⁻¹ and out-of-plane C–H bends at 750, 805 and 860 cm⁻¹ – all typical of a single-substituted phenyl ring.  
• Intense carbonyl band at 1790 cm⁻¹ matches the high-frequency ν(C=O) of an acid chloride (≈1780–1810 cm⁻¹), which is present only in candidate 1 (phenyl chloroformate, O=C(Cl)O-Ph).  
• Medium bands at 1167 and 1187 cm⁻¹ are consistent with C–O stretches of an aryl chloroformate.  
• Low-frequency bands at 505–620 cm⁻¹ fall in the region for C–Cl stretches, again expected for an acid chloride.  

Other candidates either lack an aromatic ring (2-4, 9) or a carbonyl (10), or possess different ring systems whose Raman signatures do not feature the characteristic 1000 cm⁻¹ ring-breathing plus 1790 cm⁻¹ carbonyl chloride band. Therefore candidate 1 best fits the observed peaks.
